title: Handling Request Bodies with @RequestBody
description: Send JSON data to your API and map it to Java objects.

slides.title: Receiving Data in the Request Body 📦
slides.content:
# When to Use @RequestBody

For POST, PUT, PATCH requests, the data is often sent in the body of the request (as JSON, XML, etc.). Spring can automatically convert that data into a Java object using **HttpMessageConverter**.

You don’t need to parse the JSON yourself – just annotate a parameter with `@RequestBody` and Spring does the rest.

quizData.question: Which annotation tells Spring to map the HTTP request body to a Java object?
quizData.explanation: @RequestBody is used to bind the HTTP request body to a method parameter.

slides.title: Sending a Request
slides.content:
A client would send a POST request with JSON body:

```json
{
  "name": "Alice",
  "email": "alice@example.com"
}
```

Spring maps the JSON fields to the `User` object’s fields (by name).
